title: AI Gateway logs now show session affinity
description: AI Gateway logs now have a Sessions view that groups requests into sessions and shows how session affinity routed each one. Each row shows the coding agent or app that ran the session, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, along with its cost, models, providers, and how much of its input was cached across every turn. Open a session to see its cache hit rate, duration, and path. The path lists each turn with its model and timing, and names the provider serving the session along with any earlier ones. Session affinity sends each turn to the provider that served the one before it, so the provider already has most of the prompt in cache. A session that stays on one provider reads more of each prompt from cache . Filter sessions by turns, client, model, provider, authentication, or cost. Single-turn sessions are hidden until you clear the minimum turns filter. Session affinity runs by default on text and chat requests. To group requests yourself, send the same sessionId in providerOptions.gateway , or the same x-session-id header, on every request in a conversation. Requests without one are grouped by a fingerprint of the conversation's opening and appear as fingerprinted sessions. Read the session affinity documentation for more information on how AI Gateway identifies sessions. Read more

title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 now available on AI Gateway
description: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is now available on AI Gateway . DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash that improves reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and image understanding. The coding gains show up in terminal work and in building and editing whole repositories, and the agentic gains in multi-step automation. With images, the model reads charts and handles visual reasoning more accurately when it can call tools. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 also finishes tasks faster and with shorter outputs than the previous snapshot, so agent runs tend to take less time and use fewer output tokens. Use deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 as the model name: To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Try DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 in the model playground . AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting , Zero Data Retention support , budgets for API keys , routing rules , and more. AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. You can view all language models available on AI Gateway. Read more

title: Elorian AI's Glimpse now available on AI Gateway
description: Glimpse from Elorian is now available on AI Gateway. The visual reasoning model accepts images and video to follow objects through motion, interpret spatial relationships, and connect an action to its physical consequences. Glimpse can return to visual evidence as it works: zooming into a detail, revisiting a short interval of video, or tracking the same feature across frames. This allows the model to support use cases like scientific chart analysis, video captioning, visual counting, and robotics data annotation. Some examples include checking a train's motion to determine whether it is slowing down, keeping objects distinct through camera movement, and labeling completed actions in robot footage. Use elorian/glimpse as the model name: With AI SDK 7, you can send a video as a file part. Replace the placeholder URL with a public or signed HTTPS URL for your video: To configure AI Gateway in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup: Try Glimpse in the model playground . title: Introducing Token Pass
description: Vercel Token Pass is now in early access for Pro teams. For $30 per month, your team gets $80 in monthly credit for GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3, with more models to come. Use Token Pass with coding agents such as fx, Command Code, and Pi, or build your own personal agent with the AI SDK. Token Pass runs through AI Gateway , so you can choose your tools and switch between included models using your team’s shared credit. Token Pass has Zero Data Retention (ZDR) enabled by default. Requests run through selected providers with inference in the US and EU. AI Gateway and the provider delete your prompts and responses after each request, and your prompts aren’t used to train models. To get started: Open the Token Pass page in your team’s AI Gateway dashboard. Activate your subscription, create a Token Pass API key, and follow the setup instructions to connect your agent. Select GLM 5.3 or Kimi K3, and start building. The subscription renews monthly unless canceled. Unused credit doesn’t roll over. When your credit runs out, Token Pass requests stop until the next billing period, with no automatic overage charges. Learn more in the Token Pass documentation. Read more

title: Vercel Daemons is now in public beta
description: Vercel Daemons is now in public beta, allowing you to run long-running processes that pull and execute work from Vercel Queues , databases, or third-party systems without requiring an HTTP server: Consumers using Vercel Queues poll mode , Celery, BullMQ, RabbitMQ, or Kafka. Temporal or Cadence workers that long-poll their task queues. Self-hosted CI runners for GitHub Actions, GitLab, or CircleCI that poll for jobs without requiring inbound connections. Daemons run containers on Fluid compute and deploy alongside your app in the same project. Vercel builds your image and maintains the instance count you configure in each region, restarting instances that exit or crash. Get started by packaging your application and dependencies in a Dockerfile or Containerfile, then adding a daemons entry to one configuration file at your project root. This example uses worker/Dockerfile to run one Celery worker in iad1 (Washington, D.C.): Set any connection details your worker needs in your project's production environment variables, then deploy to production. Vercel starts the configured instances, and their output appears in your project's Logs . CPU and memory metrics are available with Observability Plus . Learn more in the Vercel Daemons documentation . Read more
